Tip1: Right-click a column header to sort its tickets — by title, priority, assignee or date. The choice is shared between the home kanban and the project board.
Tip2: Drag a ticket onto another one to turn it into a sub-ticket. The 📂 badge on the parent opens its own sub-kanban.
Tip3: Ctrl+Z undoes your last board actions — moves, deletes, renames, priority changes — up to 30 steps back.
Tip4: The search understands tokens: #42, @assignee, priority:critical, label:bug, by:owner, or >2026-03-01 for dates.
Tip5: Schedule a ticket with ⏰ and it will move to its target column by itself when the time comes.
Tip6: The home has two views, each with its own URL: the unified kanban at / and the project cards at /projects. Bookmark the one you prefer.
Tip7: Automations can call external services with the httpRequest action — placeholders like {ticketId}, {ticketTitle} or {now} are filled in for you.
Tip8: Chat with a ticket's assigned agent straight from the ticket panel — the 💬 button keeps the ticket as context.
Tip9: KittyClaw has no authentication and its agents run code on this machine. Keep it on localhost — never expose the port through a tunnel or reverse proxy.
Tip10: Pause a project with ⏸ to stop its automations. Paused projects sink to the bottom of the home, collapsed.
Tip11: Paste an image directly into a description or comment editor — it is uploaded and linked automatically.
Tip12: Write #42 in a comment to link a ticket, or #project-slug:7 to reference a ticket in another project.
Tip13: Everything you see in the UI is scriptable: the REST API is documented live at /api/docs.
Tip14: Esc closes overlays layer by layer — dropdown first, then editor, then panel. No mouse needed.
